section_summary: This section contains multiple copies and fragments of the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo's monthly report on conditions in Japan for July 1941 (Despatch No. 5812 transmitting Report No. 1677). The documents detail Japan's military penetration into southern French Indochina, the subsequent retaliatory freezing of Japanese assets by the United States, Great Britain, Canada, and the Netherlands East Indies, and the Japanese bombing at Chungking that endangered the gunboat USS Tutuila. It also covers major domestic developments, notably the dissolution of the Second Konoye Cabinet to drop Foreign Minister Yosuke Matsuoka following the German invasion of the Soviet Union, the formation of the Third Konoye Cabinet, and large-scale military and economic mobilization.

subfiles.about: Continuation of Embassy Tokyo's monthly report on political, foreign, and economic affairs in Japan during July 1941.
subfiles.summary: This concluding portion of the monthly report covers the termination of commercial treaties and freezing of Japanese assets by Britain and Canada, Axis recognition of the Wang Ching-wei regime at Nanking, and Japan's military occupation of air and naval bases in southern French Indochina under an agreement with Vichy France. It details the Netherlands East Indies asset freeze and export embargo, Japanese diplomatic reorientation following the German attack on the USSR, and vast domestic mobilization with troop movements to Manchuria. It also reports on the resignation of the Second Konoye Cabinet to replace Foreign Minister Matsuoka, the composition of the Third Konoye Cabinet, and the severe economic shock caused by Allied financial freezes and bad domestic harvests.
subfiles.title: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of July, 1941 (Report No. 1677) [Continuation]

subfiles.about: Embassy Tokyo's full monthly report for July 1941 regarding Japanese foreign relations, internal politics, and economic conditions, transmitted by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits the Embassy's comprehensive confidential report on conditions in Japan during July 1941, complete with chronological registers of all telegrams and despatches sent to the State Department during the month. The report documents Japan's aggressive advance into southern French Indochina, the resulting retaliatory asset-freezing orders imposed by the United States, Britain, and the Dutch East Indies, and the diplomatic crisis caused by the Japanese aerial bombing near the USS Tutuila at Chungking. Additionally, it examines the political fallout from the outbreak of the German-Soviet war, the cabinet reconstruction that removed Foreign Minister Yosuke Matsuoka in favor of Admiral Teijiro Toyoda, and comprehensive domestic economic regimentation and military mobilization.
